newsitem.title: CHINA: China parliament shows dissatisfaction over crime.
newsitem.headline: China parliament shows dissatisfaction over crime.

text.p: China's usually docile parliament showed its dissatisfaction with the government's battle against crime on Friday, with about 40 percent of deputies declining to approve the top prosecutor's report.

The displeasure with the report by the chief procurator marked the lowest ever show of support for a government report, with 1,621 voting for while 675 voted against, 390 abstaining and 34 casting no vote.
It was the largest proportion of protest votes on record by the usually rubber-stamp National People's Congress, with a support rate of 59.6 percent.

In his report this week, Procurator General Zhang Siqing said prosecutors had boosted the number of arrests by about 17 percent last year, but much remained to be done to rein in a tide of lawbreaking.
Violent crime, narcotics offences and gang and mafia-style criminal activity remained rampant, he said and warned that "hostile foreign forces were trying to Westernise and split China".
